1 رَمَقَهُ , (S, Mgh, K,) aor.
رَمُقَ , (S, Mgh,) inf. n. رَمْقٌ, (S,) He looked at him, or it; (S, TA;) as also ↓رَامقهُ: (TA:) or he glanced lightly at him, or it; looked at him, or it, lightly, from the outer angle of the eye: (IDrd, K, TA:) or he looked long at him, or it; (Mgh;) or so رَمَقَهُ بِعَيْنِهِ, aor. and inf. n. as above: (Msb:) whence, in a trad., فَرَمَقَهُ النَّاسُ بِأَبْصَارهِمْ [And the people looked long at him]: (Mgh:) or رَمَقْتُهُ بِبَصَرِى and ↓ رَامَقْتُهُ signify I followed him with my eye, paying attention to him, and watching him: (TA:) and ↓ رامقهُ , (TA,) inf. n. رِمَاقٌ, (K, * TA,) he looked at him from the outer angle of the eye with a look of enmity: (K, * TA:) and ↓ رمّقهُ , inf. n. تَرْميقٌ, he looked at him long from the outer angle of the eye with anger or aversion: (TA:) and ↓ رمّق , inf. n. as above, he continued looking; like رنّق. (S, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
